what: One head call per batch instead of one per row, on Apple Metal (MPS).
how: Same process, same synthetic batch, same optimizer: the row-by-row path (`row_logits` in a Python loop) against `PointerDecisionHead.forward_batch`. Median of 5 steps after 2 warm-up steps. GPU utilisation sampled every 250 ms from ioreg IOAccelerator `Device Utilization %` (max across accelerators), not estimated.
machine: Apple M4 Max 48 GB, device mps

profile_before.note: Where a step's wallclock went with the row loop (B=64, last-n, under contention).

findings: The row loop leaves the GPU at ~50-60 % mean utilisation whatever the batch size: it is dispatch-bound, so a bigger batch buys nothing (51-56 samples/s at B=64, 128 and 256 alike).
Batched, throughput scales with the batch again and the device saturates: 97.4 % mean at B=128.
B=128 is the throughput optimum on this machine; B=256 regresses (163 vs 183 samples/s) under memory pressure.
The running anti-scaling experiments stay at B=64 on purpose - changing the batch size would change the optimisation, and the whole 250k-1M curve family was measured at 64.

equivalence.claim: forward_batch equals forward row by row to 1e-5 with ragged option sets and a padded state, and the content of a padding slot cannot reach a real row.
